name: Webhook reliability: retry with exponential backoff

parameters.content:
## Retry with exponential backoff
Receives a JSON POST and forwards it to your target URL. Failures are retried with a doubling delay plus jitter. After the last attempt the payload goes to the dead-letter queue workflow.

### How it works
1. The webhook answers at once with n8n's immediate acknowledgement. The caller does not get the delivery result.
2. `Call Target` POSTs the payload. Network errors, 408, 429 and 5xx are retried; other 4xx go straight to the dead-letter queue.
3. Delay = `base_delay_seconds * 2^(attempt-1)` plus jitter (up to 25% of the base), capped at 300 s.
4. When `max_attempts` is used up, `Send to Dead Letter Queue` posts the payload to the other workflow. If that call fails, the payload can be lost.

### Setup
1. Before activating, enable Header Auth on the Webhook node. These webhooks are unauthenticated by default.
2. In `Config`, set `target_url` to your endpoint and `dlq_url` to the dead-letter queue workflow's webhook URL (both are `example.invalid` placeholders and will not work until replaced). Optionally change `base_delay_seconds` and `max_attempts`.
3. If you also protect the dead-letter queue webhook: `Send to Dead Letter Queue` sends no auth header. Select the same n8n credential on that node, or the hand-off fails.

Tested headless on n8n 2.35.7 (2026-10-13); not yet imported through the editor UI by a human. Test steps and limits: README.md and TESTING.md at https://github.com/claude-farm-hq/n8n-webhook-reliability

## Receive and configure
The webhook answers at once. `Config` holds your URLs and retry limits.

## Call the target
POSTs the payload. A 2xx response counts as delivered.

## Retry or hand off
On failure: work out the delay, wait, call again. After the last attempt, send the payload to the dead-letter queue.
